channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Motta diz que ida do PT à Justiça é direito, mas defende dosimetria
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta said the PT has the right to appeal to the STF against the overturning of Lula’s veto on the dosimetry law for January 8 crimes, but stressed that Congress’s decision should be upheld. He called the bill a chance for national pacification. The law benefits Jair Bolsonaro and 849 others convicted in the 2023 attacks.

item.title: Após derrota dupla no Congresso, Lula falta aos 200 anos da Câmara
item.description: President Lula did not attend the Chamber's 200th anniversary ceremony following two congressional defeats: the rejection of Jorge Messias for the Supreme Court and the overturning of his veto on the Dosimetry Bill. He was represented by Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães before traveling to the U.S. to meet with Donald Trump. His absence highlights the growing disconnect between the Planalto and Congress in 2026, with no recorded meetings with congressional leaders so far this year.

item.title: Por encontro com Trump, Lula embarca para os Estados Unidos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva departed for the United States on Wednesday to meet with Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday. The meeting aims to restore trade relations strained by U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods and will cover cooperation against organized crime, critical minerals, geopolitics, and Brazilian elections. Lula noted Vice President Geraldo Alckmin will assume presidential duties during his absence.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro pode se lançar a suplente de senador mesmo vivendo nos EUA?
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro plans to run as a Senate substitute for São Paulo while living in the U.S., despite being stripped of office and facing criminal charges at the STF for coercion related to the coup attempt. Although there is no immediate legal barrier, his candidacy hinges on the timing of a final conviction: if upheld before the election, it could trigger supervenient ineligibility and block his diploma.

item.title: Especialista explica o que muda para Bolsonaro após derrubada de veto ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: The overturning of the presidential veto on the Dosimetria Bill allows for sentence reduction for those convicted in the January 8 acts, including Jair Bolsonaro, through the application of beneficial retroactivity in criminal law. However, constitutional expert Acácio Miranda notes that the new law requires a formal manifestation from the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to grant benefits, making the process more bureaucratic and a rapid release unlikely — Bolsonaro is expected to remain imprisoned for at least three or four years. President Lula’s decision not to promulgate the law leaves room for political and judicial debate, while a potential future amnesty by another president could change the scenario, though this falls outside the scope of the Dosimetria Bill discussion.

item.title: Hugo Motta é contra a criação de estatal para minerais críticos
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta opposed the creation of a state-owned company, Terrabras, to explore critical minerals, advocating instead for strengthening the National Council of Mineral Policy and Rare Earths as a means to ensure national sovereignty without compromising private investment. He argued that the council model fulfills the government’s strategy of maintaining state control over strategic resources without establishing a public enterprise. The Terrabras proposal, initially considered by the Lula administration, was postponed and has since lost momentum, with current focus shifting to regulatory adjustments and export restriction mechanisms.

item.title: Desenrola cria cultura que ignora razão do endividamento recorde, diz pesquisador do 'Brasil dos boletos'
item.description: Researcher Kauê Lopes dos Santos from 'Brasil dos boletos' states that while the Desenrola 2.0 program is an important government response to indebtedness, it may foster a culture of debt renegotiation that overlooks structural causes of credit dependency in Brazil, focusing only on short-term solutions.

item.title: Ministro da articulação política de Lula se reúne com Alcolumbre uma semana após derrota de Messias
item.description: Political Articulation Minister José Guimarães met with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to ease tensions between the Lula government and Congress, one week after the defeat of Jorge Messias in the STF nomination and the overturning of the Dosimetry bill veto. The meeting aimed to 'turn the page' on recent parliamentary setbacks, with Guimarães stressing that the government is not over and advocating for calm, non-resentful engagement.

item.title: Depois de reveses, Guimarães elogia convivência democrática na Câmara
item.description: Minister José Guimarães praised democratic coexistence in the Chamber of Deputies during the 200th anniversary celebration, highlighting his 20 years as a federal deputy and emphasizing that Parliament has overcome difficult moments, such as the Military Dictatorship and January 8. He made these remarks following two legislative defeats for the Lula government: the Senate’s rejection of Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF and Congress overturning Lula’s veto on the Dosimetria bill, which reduces penalties for coup-related crimes.

item.title: Governador interino do RJ é aprovado por 52,9%, diz pesquisa
item.description: The Futura/Apex poll shows that interim Rio de Janeiro Governor Ricardo Couto has 52.9% approval and 38.5% disapproval, with 31.6% rating his administration as excellent or good. Conducted between April 22–24 among 1,000 voters, the survey has a 3.1-point margin of error and 95% confidence level. Couto assumed office following resignations in the succession line, including former Governor Cláudio Castro, and his continuation in office was ordered by STF Minister Cristiano Zanin, pending a decision on a supplementary election by January 2027.

item.title: Pilili, a inútil
item.description: The TSE launched Pilili, an electronic ballot box mascot, to celebrate 30 years of electronic voting and engage younger voters. Though visually simple and childlike, the initiative aims to make the electoral process more accessible and playful for new generations. The post criticizes the mascot as 'useless' and overly juvenile, likening it to kindergarten-level design.

item.title: Lula deixa Brasília e decola para encontro com Trump na Casa Branca
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva departed for Washington on Wednesday afternoon to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday. The agenda includes discussions on trade tariffs, the potential designation of Brazilian criminal factions as terrorist organizations, the war in Iran, critical mineral exploration, and the situation in Venezuela. Lula is accompanied by ministers of Foreign Affairs, Justice, Finance, Development, Mines and Energy, and the director-general of the Federal Police.

item.title: É #FAKE que Lula disse que 'vai embora para Cuba' se Flávio Bolsonaro vencer eleições
item.description: False posts circulating on social media claim President Lula said he would 'move to Cuba' if Flávio Bolsonaro wins the 2026 presidential election. There is no official record of such a statement, and the Presidency’s Secretariat of Communication (Secom) has denied it outright. In an interview with Der Spiegel, Lula stated he would accept the people's decision, regardless of the outcome.

item.title: Participação de adolescentes no eleitorado pode atingir pior nível desde 2014, segundo projeção
item.description: The deadline for issuing voter IDs ends this Wednesday (June 6), and Brazil is projected to record the lowest participation rate of 16- and 17-year-olds in a presidential election since at least 2014. This low youth engagement may reflect political disaffection, lack of information, or bureaucratic barriers, affecting the representativeness of the electorate.

item.title: Motta diz que Câmara dará 'grande contribuição' para acordo entre Lula e Trump se aprovar projeto sobre terras-raras
item.description: Hugo Motta, president of the Chamber of Deputies, stated that approving the National Critical Minerals Policy — which includes up to R$5 billion in fiscal incentives and a R$2 billion guarantee fund — would be a 'major contribution' to Lula-Trump negotiations on rare earths. Reporter Arnaldo Jardim called the bill a 'trump card' in talks with the U.S., noting it creates favorable rules for foreign investment and technology transfer. The bill is set for vote Wednesday, with rare earths expected to be discussed in the Lula-Trump meeting Thursday.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro reforça defesa de redução de maioridade penal com gradações de 14 e 16 anos
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for President of Brazil, reinforced his defense of lowering the age of criminal responsibility in Brazil, proposing graduated thresholds of 14 and 16 years. His statements align with a broader agenda of penal hardening, consistent with his political faction's positions.

item.title: Judiciário e Legislativo “não se enfrentam”, diz Ministro Edson Fachin
item.description: Supreme Court and National Justice Council President Edson Fachin stated that the Judiciary and Legislature do not confront or replace each other, but must operate independently and harmoniously to ensure the legitimacy of the democratic state. Speaking during a solemn session at the Chamber of Deputies marking the House’s 200th anniversary, he emphasized institutional independence as essential for effectiveness and legitimacy. His remarks came amid congressional criticism of STF justices over the Banco Master case, which has triggered impeachment requests and calls for a parliamentary inquiry.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: Os três fatores que podem definir o vencedor, segundo CEO de instituto de pesquisa
item.description: Cila Schulmann, CEO of the Ideia Research Institute, identified cost of living, online betting, and indebtedness as the three decisive factors in the 2026 presidential election between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. She emphasized that approximately 5 million non-polarized voters, concentrated in urban Southeast regions, could be the swing bloc, favoring concrete economic proposals over ideological debates.

item.title: Conselho de Ética suspende três deputados por motim na Câmara
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Ethics Council suspended the mandates of deputies Marcos Pollon (PL-MS), Marcel van Hattem (Novo-RS), and Zé Trovão (PL-SC) for 60 days due to breach of decorum, following a protest in favor of amnesty for those convicted in the January 8, 2023 attacks. The suspension requires plenary confirmation with at least 257 votes, and the deputies may appeal to the CCJ.

item.title: Lula e Trump podem mostrar as cartas em relação a minerais críticos, big techs e tarifas
item.description: Lula and Trump are set to meet in Washington to discuss critical minerals, big techs, and organized crime, in a meeting seen as an opportunity for Lula to shift focus from recent domestic political defeats. However, advisors warn that careful messaging is needed due to Trump’s controversial image and the risk of further political backlash. The meeting occurs amid mutual distrust, with the U.S. suspected of employing an ambiguous strategy to extract economic and political gains from Brazil, while the Brazilian government seeks to preserve dialogue channels without yielding to external pressure.

item.title: Ao vivo: Câmara vota o marco dos minerais críticos
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies is voting on a bill to establish the National Policy for Critical and Strategic Minerals, including a up to R$5 billion guarantee fund to reduce credit risks and boost domestic investment. The vote, originally scheduled for Tuesday, was postponed at the request of mining companies and now takes place on Wednesday, May 6, 2026, with government support. The issue will also be discussed in the upcoming meeting between President Lula and Donald Trump in Washington D.C. on Thursday, May 7, 2026, continuing bilateral talks that began in 2025.

item.title: Governo Lula não quis regular venda de terras raras em Goiás
item.description: The sale of Serra Verde, a rare earths miner in Goiás, in April 2026, involved only a transfer of control between foreign entities (Denham Capital, Energy & Minerals Group, and Vision Blue Resources to USA Rare Earth), not the sale of a Brazilian company. The federal government, not the state, holds exclusive authority over mining concessions and foreign investment review in strategic assets, and did not intervene in the transaction. The Lula administration's narrative that Brazil is being handed over to foreign capital is factually incorrect, as Serra Verde was never Brazilian-owned.

item.title: Perfil político ou técnico? Como os brasileiros acham que deve ser a escolha do novo ministro do STF
item.description: According to Meio/Ideia poll, 39.4% of Brazilians prefer Lula to appoint a technically qualified, non-government-linked nominee to the STF, while 37% support a government-affiliated pick like Jorge Messias. An additional 5% want a woman appointed regardless of profile. The Senate’s rejection of Messias is interpreted by 36% as opposition sabotage, 35% as a government defeat, and 12% as the Senate fulfilling its constitutional role.

item.title: Pesquisa mostra o número que mais dificulta o avanço de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre Lula
item.description: Lula leads with 40% of voting intentions in the first round, against 36% for Flávio Bolsonaro, with stronger voter loyalty: 72.8% of Lula’s supporters have already decided their vote, compared to only 56.9% of Flávio’s. The research shows a consistent shift of Bolsonaro’s political capital to Flávio, who is spontaneously mentioned by 20% versus 4% for Jair Bolsonaro, but his national recognition remains limited by reliance on his father’s name, hindering conversion to firm support.

item.title: Temer diz ser “inteiramente favorável” à dosimetria
item.description: Former President Michel Temer said he is entirely in favor of the dosimetry bill, which reduces sentences for coup d'état and abolition of the rule of law offenses, benefiting Jair Bolsonaro and 849 others convicted for the January 8, 2023 attacks. He praised Congress for upholding the bill’s integrity, stating it aims at national pacification, with the STF to review cases individually. Temer also expressed regret over Jorge Messias’s rejection to the STF, calling him a qualified jurist, and endorsed a potential Lula-Trump meeting as useful and appropriate for multilateralism.

item.title: Múcio se reúne com Alcolumbre após Senado rejeitar Messias e diz não ser o momento de Lula indicar outro nome ao STF
item.description: Defense Minister José Múcio Monteiro met with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to ease tensions following the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF. Múcio stated that now is not the time to present a new nominee and that the priority is to lower political tensions. The government views the meeting as an initial step to rebuild dialogue with Congress after a historic defeat.

item.title: A disputa entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno em 10 estados, segundo a Quaest
item.description: The Quaest poll conducted between April 21 and 28, 2026, across ten states shows Lula leading in Bahia, Pernambuco, Ceará, Pará, and Minas Gerais, while Flávio Bolsonaro leads in Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Goiás, Paraná, and Rio Grande do Sul. The race is tight in Minas Gerais and Pará, with margins within the margin of error. The survey included 11,646 voters with a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Título de eleitor: termina hoje prazo para tirar documento e regularizar situação eleitoral
item.description: The deadline to obtain a first voter ID, transfer electoral domicile, update registration data, and resolve electoral pendencies ends this Wednesday (6). After this date, individuals not in good standing with the Electoral Justice will be unable to vote in the October 2026 general elections, which will elect the president, governors, deputies, and senators. Remote service is available via the TSE website, except for first-time voter registration and biometrics, which require in-person attendance.

item.title: Governo reduz juros e amplia prazo de pagamento de programa para financiar reformas da casa
item.description: The government reduced interest rates for the Minha Casa, Minha Vida home renovation program from 1.95% to 0.82% per month and extended the repayment term from 60 to 72 months. The measure aims to align monthly payments with the budgets of families earning up to R$9,600, allowing loans between R$5,000 and R$30,000 for labor, materials, and technical assistance, with payments capped at 25% of household income. The extension creates an implicit subsidy of approximately R$567 million, already budgeted.

item.title: Lula levará cinco ministros e diretor da PF em visita a Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will travel to the United States to meet with former President Donald Trump, accompanied by five federal ministers and the director-general of the Federal Police, Andrei Rodrigues. The meeting takes place amid ongoing diplomatic and economic tensions between Brazil and the U.S., with a focus on cooperation in security, trade, and migration.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: como está a aprovação de Lula nos maiores colégios eleitorais do Brasil
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll conducted from April 21 to 28, 2026, surveyed 11,646 voters across 562 municipalities and found that President Lula maintains approval above 50% in Brazil’s three largest Northeastern electoral colleges: Bahia (60%), Pernambuco (61%), and Ceará (58%). In the North’s largest college, Pará, he reached 49% approval — still above disapproval at 45%. In all other surveyed states, disapproval exceeds approval, with the widest gaps in Paraná (60% disapproval vs 34% approval), Goiás (61% vs 37%), and São Paulo (58% vs 37%).

item.title: Leia os focos dos EUA na investigação comercial contra o Brasil
item.description: The U.S. is investigating Brazilian trade practices under Section 301 of the Trade Act, focusing on ethanol tariffs, the Central Bank's dual role as Pix operator and regulator, digital laws, deforestation, and forced labor. The September 2025 hearing highlighted complaints about Pix's competitive advantages and barriers to U.S. ethanol in RenovaBio, seeking greater transparency and fair competition.

item.title: Governo Lula é desaprovado em 6 de 10 Estados, diz Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released on May 6, 2026, shows that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) is disapproved by a majority in 6 of the 10 surveyed states: Minas Gerais, Rio Grande do Sul, São Paulo, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro, and Goiás. He is approved in Pernambuco, Bahia, Ceará, and Pará. The margin of error ranges from 2 to 3 percentage points, with a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Defensoria volta a dizer que Moraes violou direitos de Tagliaferro
item.description: The Federal Public Defender's Office (DPU) filed a new petition yesterday alleging that Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the STF violated the rights of Eduardo Tagliaferro, a former TSE employee. The DPU claims Moraes’s actions against Tagliaferro breach constitutional guarantees, including the right to defense and due process. The petition reinforces prior concerns raised by the DPU about the minister’s conduct in cases involving public servants.

item.title: A avaliação do ministro da Fazenda sobre possível recuo na ‘taxa das blusinhas’
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that the Lula government is discussing a possible review of the 'blusinhas tax,' which imposes a 20% Import Tax on international purchases under $50, but stressed that it will not abandon the Remessa Conforme program. He noted the program enables better oversight, including blocking harmful or Anvisa-controlled products, and emphasized that while he is open to rational debate, preserving the program's advances is non-negotiable.

item.title: Lula autoriza Rio a renegociar dívida e parcelas devem cair mais de R$ 370 milhões
item.description: The federal government authorized Rio de Janeiro to exit the Fiscal Recovery Regime and join the Propag program, reducing monthly debt payments to the Union from about R$490 million to roughly R$113 million — a monthly savings of over R$370 million. The agreement allows up to 30 years to settle the debt and ties the financial relief to strategic investments in technical education, state universities, sanitation, housing, transportation, public security, and climate change adaptation.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula viaja para tentar engambelar Trump
item.description: President Lula is traveling to the United States for a meeting with Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday, November 7, to discuss economic and security issues, including cooperation against criminal organizations. Vice President Geraldo Alckmin confirmed the goal is to establish a bilateral agreement on crime-fighting efforts.

item.title: Lula leva 5 ministros para reunião com Trump
item.description: President Lula will bring five ministers and the director-general of the Federal Police to a meeting with Donald Trump at the White House on May 7, 2026, focusing on combating organized crime and trade issues, including potential discussion of rare earth minerals. Although the CV and PCC are not priorities for terrorist designation, the meeting aims to deepen bilateral cooperation following a postponement due to disagreements over the Iran war. Lula is expected to return to Brazil the same day.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro repete preferência de voto de Jair em 2022, diz diretor da Quaest; veja números em 10 estados
item.description: According to Quaest director Felipe Nunes, Flávio Bolsonaro's polling performance in 2026 mirrors his father Jair Bolsonaro's 2022 vote share, with a slight advantage for the opposition over Lula. Flávio is polling better than Jair did in 2022 in São Paulo, Ceará, and the Southern states, while Lula makes up ground in Minas Gerais and Pernambuco. In the other surveyed states (RJ, BA, PA, GO), the situation remains largely unchanged from 2022.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: os estados em que o bolsonarismo mais avançou com a campanha de Flávio
item.description: The entry of Flávio Bolsonaro as the new leader of the bolsonarismo resulted in electoral advances in six of Brazil's largest electoral colleges, according to Genial/Quaest poll. In São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, there was a slight recovery after the 2022 decline, while in Rio Grande do Sul, bolsonarism surpassed its 2018 peak. In historically unfavorable states like Pará, Ceará, and Bahia, the movement showed gradual improvement, though still below 50%.

item.title: O que a mobilização do voto jovem ensina sobre comunicação pública no Brasil
item.description: The mobilization of young voters in Brazil's 2022 elections showed that institutional communication must adapt to young people's digital habits by using relatable language, memes, and partnerships with platforms and influencers, rather than traditional approaches. Led by the TSE under Minister Edson Fachin, the strategy focused on simplifying access through Título Net and organically engaging artists and personalities, reversing the historically low registration of 16- and 17-year-olds. This experience reveals that effective public communication requires presence in the digital spaces where the audience already is, with authenticity and cultural relevance.

item.title: Escala 6x1: Motta defende redução da jornada de trabalho e diz que Congresso deve definir neste mês tamanho do corte
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta advocated for reducing the workweek from 44 to 40 hours as part of the debate to end the 6x1 work scale. He emphasized that the issue should be defined in Congress this month, with a vote scheduled for May 26 in the Special Committee, and stressed the importance of using a Constitutional Amendment Proposal (PEC) to ensure broad debate and avoid electoral influence, given the upcoming October elections.

item.title: Lula é desaprovado em SP, RJ, MG e mais 3 Estados; aprovação é maior em 4 Estados
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva shows higher disapproval than approval in Goiás, Paraná, São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Rio Grande do Sul, and Minas Gerais, with Goiás recording the highest disapproval at 61%. In contrast, Pernambuco, Bahia, Ceará, and Pará show approval exceeding disapproval, with Pernambuco leading at 61% approval. Nationally, 52% disapprove and 43% approve of the government, while overall evaluation is negative in 42% of cases.

item.title: Lula x família Bolsonaro: estados populosos têm cenários parecidos com o resultado de 2022, aponta pesquisa Genial/Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows that, in ten populous states, the 2026 electoral landscape mirrors the 2022 result between Lula and the Bolsonaro family. Lula slightly improved in Minas Gerais and Pernambuco, while Flávio Bolsonaro outperforms Jair Bolsonaro in São Paulo, Ceará, and Rio Grande do Sul, with widened advantages. Rio de Janeiro remains stable, with Flávio leading by 16 points — two more than his father in 2022.

item.title: Pilili é uma ideia
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unveiled the mascot Pilili, inspired by the sound of the electronic ballot box after vote confirmation, to celebrate 30 years of the technology. The initiative aims to bring electoral justice closer to the public, especially youth, in a playful and accessible way.

item.title: Soluções consensuais em revisão
item.description: The TCU continues advancing the consolidation of consensual solutions despite uncertainty from initial votes in ADPF 1183 at the STF. The recent normative update via IN 102/2026, inspired by remarks from ministers Flávio Dino and Edson Fachin, introduced a review mechanism for TCU Presidency decisions. Acórdão 850/2026-P reinforced this trend by suggesting improvements to IN 91/2022, including greater legal security, formalized timelines, and robust motivation for credit discounts, showing the TCU remains active in evolving the procedure even under judicial scrutiny.

item.title: Durigan diz que Lula e Trump discutirão tarifas e crime organizado
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said the upcoming meeting between Lula and Trump in Washington will address tariffs, bilateral trade, and organized crime. He noted Brazil runs a trade deficit with the U.S. when digital and financial services are included, contrary to the belief of a surplus. The agenda also covers critical minerals, rare earths, and a U.S. Section 301 investigation into Brazilian trade practices.

item.title: ‘Não posso tentar ser igual a ele’, diz Flávio Bolsonaro ao se diferenciar do pai
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro said he is working to establish his own political identity, distinct from his father Jair Bolsonaro’s style, emphasizing moderation, articulation, and negotiated solutions. He noted that increased public exposure has helped voters see him as different from his father, focused on dialogue and keeping agreements, and claimed he is fully prepared to run for president in 2026.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Flávio Bolsonaro vence em SP, RJ e mais 3 Estados, e Lula, em 4, com empate em MG
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leads Lula in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Rio Grande do Sul, Paraná and two other states, while the president wins in four states including Bahia, with a technical tie in Minas Gerais. The Genial/Quaest poll shows Flávio ahead in major electoral colleges except MG, with a 26-point lead in Rio Grande do Sul and 50% to 30% in Paraná. Lula's largest advantage is in Bahia at 55% to 22%.

item.title: Durigan diz que é preciso 'afastar lobby indevido contra o PIX' em viagem de Lula aos EUA
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said the government will discuss trade tariffs and defend the Pix payment system during Lula’s meeting with Trump in Washington, stressing the need to counter undue lobbying against Pix. He also noted that 26 states have joined the imported diesel subsidy program, with only Rondonia not having formalized its participation.
